item.title: Canadian PM defends "Lake Ontario" name after Trump renaming order
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
WASHINGTON, Aug. 27 (Xinhua) -- U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday signed an executive order directing the Department of the Interior to rename Lake Ontario "Lake America," as trade tensions between the United States and Canada continue to escalate. "We're gonna to be changing the name of Lake Ontario, effective immediately, to Lake America," Trump said in the Oval Office before signing the order. The move came just two days after Trump said on social media that the United States is giving "serious consideration" to changing the name of Lake Ontario to "Lake America," citing that "we don't expect to be doing much business with Ontario any longer." Lake Ontario, one of the five Great Lakes of North America, straddles the U.S.-Canada border, with the Canadian province of Ontario to the north and the U.S. state of New York to the south. Trump's attempt to rename the lake came as a recent breakdown in trade talks between the two countries led to new retaliatory tariffs. The United States and Canada failed to reach a trade deal on Aug. 21, and the United States imposed a 50-percent tariff on about 20 billion U.S. dollars' worth of Canadian goods on Aug. 22. Canada responded by announcing "dollar-for-dollar" retaliatory tariffs on imports from the United States, set to take effect on Sept. 8. Canadian officials have already said they will not recognize the new name. Canadian Minister of Industry Melanie Joly said that Canada will always call the water body Lake Ontario. The latest executive order marks the second time Trump has challenged the longstanding name of an international body of water and unilaterally renamed it for U.S. use. On Jan. 20, 2025, the first day of his second term, Trump signed an executive order directing the renaming of the Gulf of Mexico as the "Gulf of America," a move that drew opposition from Mexico and others. At Thursday's signing event, Trump touted his earlier effort to rename the Gulf of Mexico. "We have a gulf and we have a lake. Now, all we need is an ocean. So, maybe we'll have to change the name of the Atlantic and/or the Pacific. Maybe we'll change them both," Trump said. ■

item.title: Chinese games shift from "going global" to "creating global" at Gamescom 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
* As Chinese-developed games gain wider attention from players worldwide, their distinctive Chinese cultural elements and perspectives are becoming key factors that set them apart from other games. * Chinese game companies are expanding their presence across the global gaming ecosystem. Beyond bringing more titles to international audiences, they are increasingly working with global teams and incorporating international perspectives into game development, technology and market operations. COLOGNE, Germany, Aug. 27 (Xinhua) -- Gamescom, the world's largest trade fair for computer and video games, opened on Wednesday, drawing a record number of Chinese game companies. A total of 60 Chinese companies are showcasing games and innovations at Gamescom 2026. Beyond exhibiting new creations, they are highlighting a transition from simply "going global" to genuinely "creating globally," demonstrating a deeper and more sophisticated integration into the international market. WINDOW FOR CHINESE GAMES Chinese exhibitors are presenting an expanding lineup of new products at Gamescom. Partnering with leading game studios from around the world, Tencent Games hosted an immersive game art exhibition titled "Worlds of Play," showcasing over 40 game titles, including the Chinese hit Black Myth: Wukong, as well as artworks, videos, models and interactive installations. Chinese developer NetEase Games presented its largest-ever lineup to Gamescom. Among its five self-developed titles were ANANTA, an urban open-world role-playing game, and Sea of Remnants, an ocean fantasy role-playing game, both making their global debut at the event. NetEase Games said it hopes to gather more direct feedback from overseas players, media and industry partners via Gamescom, which will help guide future development and content optimization. "Internationalization is not a single distribution step after a product is finished, but should run throughout the entire process -- from R&D and product design to localization and long-term operations," said Riten Huang, general manager of marketing at NetEase Games. During Gamescom Opening Night Live, HoYoverse unveiled Nodusfall, a cooperative action game set in a fantasy world inspired by mythologies from different cultures, including Chinese mythology documented in the ancient Classic of Mountains and Seas. Game publisher 4Divinity showcased four games in the player zone, three of which were made by Chinese studios, including The Defiant, Showa American Story and Genigods: Nezha. These games cover a wide range of genres, highlighting the diverse capabilities of Chinese game developers, said Tan Chor Yong, chief operating officer of 4Divinity. "Players now realize that Chinese games can bring highly valuable experiences to global audiences, and the next wave is heading our way," Tan said, adding that this wave of new experiences is expected to grow stronger and arrive faster in the years ahead. SHIFT TOWARD HOMEGROWN GLOBAL HITS As Chinese-developed games gain wider attention from players worldwide, their distinctive Chinese cultural elements and perspectives are becoming key factors that set them apart from other games. Igor Osadchev, a senior Unity developer at Volk Team, told Xinhua that Chinese culture is a major draw. "When I see a Chinese building or something like that, I am already interested in the game by default," he said. Chris Hewish, president of Xsolla, a global video game commerce company, has also noticed a broader transformation in the industry. Chinese studios are increasingly creating standalone hits and original intellectual property (IP) for global audiences, he said. Hewish added that many of the successful new games released over the past year have come from China rather than Western developers, marking a significant shift from the industry's historical pattern. Wanzi, head of the Hypergryph global marketing center, told Xinhua that another significant shift is underway as the global market moves from simply "seeing" Chinese games to genuinely "understanding" them. She said international audiences are increasingly looking beyond individual titles to their gameplay, storytelling, art design and technical performance, while also showing greater interest in the cultural influences and creative ideas behind them. Steve Heng, a game industry professional, believes China's mythology and ancient stories offer rich material for games with international appeal. "If you have the courage to create cool games and tell cool stories, that will resonate internationally as well," he said. More Chinese companies are transitioning from behind-the-scenes contributions to global game production to creating original IP and reaching global audiences directly, Tan said. "Further success along this path will only inspire more talent to follow suit, and this will indeed shape the global gaming market in the years to come." DEEPER GLOBAL INTEGRATION Chinese game companies are expanding their presence across the global gaming ecosystem. Beyond bringing more titles to international audiences, they are increasingly working with global teams and incorporating international perspectives into game development, technology and market operations. Grace Pan, senior project manager at Cologne Exhibition Center, noted that Chinese game companies have accelerated their global expansion after several years of adapting to international markets. She said Chinese game companies are increasingly involving international teams and incorporating perspectives at earlier stages of development, helping their games better connect with global players from the start and facilitating faster overseas expansion. "The companies are not just making great games and bringing them to global markets, but they're starting to adopt a very global development approach," Hewish said. Hewish pointed to Chinese companies setting up local offices in cities such as Toronto and Los Angeles, allowing them to stay closer to players in different markets. Technology is becoming another area where Chinese developers are contributing to the wider gaming industry. Hewish said Chinese studios have embraced artificial intelligence not only for game development but also for creating tools that can be shared across the sector. He cited Tencent's open-source AI development tools as an example. Meanwhile, the boundaries between regional gaming markets are becoming increasingly blurred. Sebastian Szczepanski, a game industry professional, said the Chinese and Western markets, once relatively separate, are now moving closer together, with publishers increasingly operating across both. Eric de Brocart, director and founder of GamerGen.com, said he hopes to establish direct ties with Chinese developers at Gamescom so that he can introduce more Chinese titles to French audiences through his website and videos. For him, perceptions are already changing. Chinese games are no longer viewed as "obscure, complicated, or too Asian to be embraced." Instead, he sees a growing number of titles that remain relatively unknown overseas but deserve wider recognition.■

item.title: Zhejiang activates highest-level emergency response as Typhoon Saudel approaches
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
This photo taken on Aug. 27, 2026 shows a locked gate at a fishing wharf in Yueqing City, east China's Zhejiang Province. East China's Zhejiang Province raised its typhoon emergency response to Level I, the highest level, at 8 p.m. Thursday as Typhoon Saudel, the 18th typhoon of this year, is forecast to make landfall in the province. (Xinhua/Han Chuanhao) HANGZHOU, Aug. 27 (Xinhua) -- East China's Zhejiang Province raised its typhoon emergency response to Level I, the highest level, at 8 p.m. Thursday as Typhoon Saudel, the 18th typhoon of this year, is forecast to make landfall in the province. At 5 p.m., the typhoon's center was located about 320 km east of Wenzhou, packing maximum wind speeds of 45 meters per second near its center. It is moving at 10 to 15 km per hour and is expected to make landfall along the coast of Zhejiang from early morning to afternoon on Friday. Hu Yaowen, chief engineer of the Zhejiang Provincial Emergency Management Department, warned that the typhoon's impact coincides with the astronomical high tide, likely creating a combination of strong winds, towering waves, high tides and heavy rainfall. He added that previous continuous heavy rains have kept rivers, lakes and reservoirs at high levels, and the new round of downpours could easily trigger mountain torrents, mudslides and landslides. To prepare for the typhoon, Zhejiang has carried out comprehensive risk inspections. More than 4,000 monitoring personnel have conducted over 19,000 patrols at more than 7,200 geological hazard potential sites and risk zones, while 564 geological experts have been dispatched to 73 counties to assist in risk identification. In terms of flood control, plain river networks across the province have drained 437 million cubic meters of water, and large and medium-sized reservoirs have pre-released 456 million cubic meters. All 14,682 marine fishing vessels in Zhejiang have taken shelter in harbors, and 47,983 crew members and 1,906 aquaculture workers have been evacuated ashore, ensuring that no people, vessels or activities remain at sea. ■ Power supply technicians inspect equipment at a fishing wharf in Yueqing City, east China's Zhejiang Province, Aug. 27, 2026. item.title: New growth drivers power China's industrial profit surge
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
BEIJING, Aug. 27 (Xinhua) -- China's burgeoning new growth drivers are fueling a sustained surge in industrial profits, reflecting the country's accelerating shift toward innovation-driven development. Profits of China's industrial firms above designated size increased 17.6 percent year on year during the first seven months of 2026, data from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) showed on Thursday. These industrial firms with an annual main business revenue of at least 20 million yuan (about 2.95 million U.S. dollars) saw their combined profits reach 4.58 trillion yuan in the January-July period, according to the data. In the three major sectors, mining industry profits jumped 34.9 percent to 666.05 billion yuan, and manufacturing profits climbed 18.8 percent to nearly 3.44 trillion yuan. However, profits in the power, heat, gas and water production and supply sector fell 5.8 percent to 478.42 billion yuan. Among major industries, the computer, communications and other electronic equipment manufacturing sector saw profits surge 110 percent. Non-ferrous metal smelting and rolling processing jumped 91.8 percent, chemical raw materials and products manufacturing rose 56.6 percent, and coal mining and washing increased 50.4 percent. The petroleum, coal and other fuel processing sector turned from losses to profits. Yu Weining, an NBS statistician, attributed the robust gains to the rapid expansion of the "AI Plus" initiative and booming demand for computing power, which boosted product demand, pushed up prices and underpinned rapid profit growth in AI-related electronic industries. Pang Ming, a researcher with the China Chief Economist Forum, said that the remarkable growth fundamentally reflects the accelerated development of new quality productive forces and the synchronized cyclical resonance of the global AI and consumer electronics industrial chains. Notably, high-end segments represented by integrated circuits, such as memory chips, have seen dividend-driven explosive growth. With the accelerated application of AI, big data, and cloud computing, the market space for the electronic information industry has expanded significantly, driving concurrent growth in upstream components and related manufacturing sectors, Pang said. Meanwhile, the recovery of export orders and the improved domestic industrial chain support have also provided solid backing for the profitability of industrial firms. Pang also noted that some traditional industries remain under pressure, highlighting the mismatch between energy costs and demand structure. The NBS data also showed that in the first seven months, the combined revenue of these industrial firms reached 80.92 trillion yuan, up 6.5 percent year on year, while operating costs increased 5.9 percent to 68.79 trillion yuan. Yu attributed the relatively fast profit growth to steady industrial production and the rapid expansion of new growth drivers. Yu highlighted the electronic sector as the main pillar, with profits surging 110 percent and contributing 9.3 percentage points to the overall industrial profit growth. High-tech manufacturing also showed strong momentum, with profits up 50.1 percent, contributing 9.6 percentage points to overall industrial profit growth. Raw material manufacturing profits rose 55.2 percent, adding 7.1 percentage points. Yu noted that the profit margin on revenue stood at 5.66 percent in the first seven months, reaching the highest level for the same period since 2023. However, Yu cautioned that the international environment remains complex and challenging, while the domestic imbalance of strong supply and weak demand is still prominent. He called for further efforts to expand domestic demand, optimize supply, and advance the upgrading of traditional industries, the growth of emerging sectors and the cultivation of future industries to consolidate the foundation for high-quality industrial development. Pang said that the industrial economy remains in a transition period characterized by the strengthening of new driving forces and the pressure on old ones. Maintaining profit momentum continues to rely on policy support and market demand recovery. In July alone, profits of major industrial firms grew 11.2 percent year on year, according to the NBS. Looking ahead, with the ongoing release of policy dividends and the deep stimulation of endogenous momentum, the performance of industrial enterprises is expected to make solid progress toward high-quality development, Pang added. ■

item.title: All affected residents, tourists evacuated following mudslide in China's Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
Evacuees from Labi Village enter a hostel in Jifu Village of Gyirong County in Xigaze, southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, Aug. 27, 2026. Residents affected by a mudslide in Gyirong County, southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, have been resettled, and all stranded tourists have been transferred, local authorities said Thursday. A total of 499 villagers and construction workers have all been properly accommodated. Meanwhile, 555 affected tourists were evacuated and transferred under the coordination of cultural and tourism authorities. No tourists remain stranded. Civil aviation authorities have also joined the rescue efforts. As of 3 p.m. Thursday, civil aviation services had transported 324 rescue personnel and delivered 24 tonnes of rescue equipment, daily necessities and medical supplies to the disaster-hit area, providing support for emergency response and the relocation of affected residents. The mudslide struck Gyirong Port in Gyirong County, Xizang, on Wednesday morning. As of 8 a.m. on Thursday, three people had been killed, 558 others remained missing, while two local villagers had been rescued. item.title: Selected works of Xi Jinping on culture published
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
BEIJING, Aug. 27 (Xinhua) -- The first and second volumes of selected works of Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on culture have been published. Compiled by the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee, the two volumes contain 78 pieces of the most important and fundamental works by Xi on cultural development from November 2012 to February 2026, which come in forms such as reports, speeches, letters and instructions. The publication is of great significance for developing a socialist culture with Chinese characteristics, igniting the cultural creativity of the entire nation, building cultural confidence and strength, and securing new successes in developing socialist culture. ■

item.title: Xi's SCO attendance, state visits to energize regional cooperation, global development
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
* Chinese President Xi Jinping will attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026 in Bishkek and pay state visits to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt from Aug. 30 to Sept. 3. * Guided by the Shanghai Spirit, the SCO has expanded from six founding members to a 27-nation family, standing out as a model for a new type of international relations. * In recent years, under the strategic guidance of the two heads of state, China and Kyrgyzstan have elevated their ties to a comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era in the spirit of solidarity and mutual benefit. * Since the establishment of diplomatic ties in 1956, China and Egypt have worked together to deepen their relationship, and strengthen friendship, solidarity and mutually beneficial cooperation. BEIJING, Aug. 27 (Xinhua) -- From Aug. 30 to Sept. 3, Chinese President Xi Jinping will attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026 in Bishkek and pay state visits to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt. Amid an ever-evolving international landscape, Xi's upcoming trip is expected to foster collaboration among all parties to deepen practical cooperation. By pooling the strengths of the Global South, it is set to advance global governance reform, promote world peace and development, and facilitate the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. CARRYING FORWARD "SHANGHAI SPIRIT" Rows of freight trains stand ready at the China-SCO Demonstration Area in Qingdao, east China's Shandong Province, awaiting departure for Central Asia and Europe -- a striking visual testament to the growing vitality of SCO cooperation. Guided by the Shanghai Spirit of mutual trust, mutual benefit, equality, consultation, respect for diverse civilizations and pursuit of common development, the SCO has expanded from six founding members to a 27-nation family. Demonstrating strong vitality and broad appeal, it has stood out as a model for a new type of international relations. "Looking back, we have weathered the storms on our journey and emerged stronger because we have adhered to the Shanghai Spirit," Xi said in his speech at the 25th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the SCO in north China's port city of Tianjin last year. Xi has attended every SCO summit since 2013, steadily shaping the grouping's development along the way. He has repeatedly called for carrying forward the "Shanghai Spirit" and forging an even closer SCO community with a shared future. At the SCO Astana summit in 2024, Xi called for building a common home featuring solidarity and mutual trust, peace and tranquility, prosperity and development, good-neighborliness and friendship, as well as fairness and justice. To further unlock the organization's potential, Xi told fellow SCO leaders at the Tianjin summit to seek common ground while shelving differences, pursue mutual benefit and win-win results, champion openness and inclusiveness, uphold fairness and justice, and strive for real results and high efficiency. Also at the Tianjin summit, the organization mapped out a strategic blueprint for its development over the next decade and ushered in a new stage of high-quality development. Over the past year, China has implemented the major initiatives proposed by Xi and contributed to regional development through concrete actions. Seven cooperation platforms -- covering green industry, digital economy, scientific and technological innovation, energy, higher education, vocational and technical education, and artificial intelligence -- have been launched, generating more than 160 projects. Meanwhile, steady implementation of the action plan for high-quality development of economic and trade cooperation continues to drive trade growth between China and SCO member states. In the process of building an SCO community with a shared future, China has been both an architect and a driving force, said Sayfiddin Juraev, a professor of political science at Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies. It is also at the Tianjin summit that Xi proposed the Global Governance Initiative, a vision that has rallied broad support across the international community. Xi's vision consistently shapes not only the SCO's current agenda but also its long-term operating strategy, Sheradil Baktygulov, director of the Kyrgyz Institute of World Politics, told Xinhua. "The SCO's values of peace, equality, and mutually beneficial cooperation are reaching the global level." NEW CHAPTER OF PARTNERSHIP China and Kyrgyzstan, linked by mountains and rivers and united by close bonds between their peoples, are good neighbors, good friends and good partners, said Xi during talks with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov in Beijing on Feb. 5, 2025. Last year marked a high point in China-Kyrgyzstan diplomacy, with the two leaders meeting three times. Key engagements also included their back-to-back meetings on the sidelines of the second China-Central Asia Summit in the Kazakh capital of Astana in June and the SCO summit in Tianjin in August. Kyrgyzstan's most valuable advantage is that it is a neighbor of China, Japarov has said. Invoking the ancient Chinese proverb -- "Amity and good-neighborliness are invaluable to a country" -- he noted that the saying aptly captures the essence of Kyrgyzstan-China relations. Since establishing diplomatic ties more than 30 years ago, China and Kyrgyzstan have been supporting each other amid shifting global dynamics. In recent years, under the strategic guidance of the two heads of state, China and Kyrgyzstan have elevated their ties to a comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era in the spirit of solidarity and mutual benefit, and are working together to build a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future featuring good-neighborliness, friendship, and shared prosperity. Practical cooperation between the two countries is gaining strong momentum, as seen in the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project, with construction well underway. In a congratulatory letter to the commencement ceremony of the project in December 2024, Xi said that the construction of the railway is a strategic decision made by the three governments to promote regional connectivity, prosperity and stability, which also reflects the shared aspiration of the three countries to open up this strategic corridor. Located in Central Asia, Kyrgyzstan was among the first countries to actively participate in Belt and Road cooperation. Projects such as the Chinese-built new North-South highway and the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan highway enhanced regional connectivity and facilitated economic exchanges. For years, China has been one of Kyrgyzstan's most important trade and investment partners, with two-way trade amounting to 27.2 billion U.S. dollars in 2025, up 19.8 percent year on year. From pure honey to fresh orchard fruit, high-quality Kyrgyz agricultural goods are becoming household favorites across China. Meanwhile, on the streets of Kyrgyzstan, sleek Chinese new-energy vehicles are quickly becoming a familiar sight. At the Irkeshtam Port on the China-Kyrgyzstan border, 24-hour freight clearance operations have helped speed up the flow of goods, streamlining cross-border trade for businesses on both sides. The port also serves as a key gateway for Chinese exports, ranging from machinery to home appliances, as they travel onward to markets across Central Asia and Europe. The bond between China and Kyrgyzstan runs deeper than trade -- it is also reflected in the growing exchange between their peoples. In Bishkek, the Luban Workshop is helping train a new generation of skilled professionals. Its curriculum standards in areas such as smart water management and electrical equipment have been incorporated into Kyrgyzstan's national education system. The two countries have also maintained close coordination on the international stage, working together within multilateral platforms such as the United Nations and the China-Central Asia mechanism. "We are witnessing one of the most meaningful and fruitful periods in the history of Kyrgyz-Chinese bilateral relations," said former Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Alikbek Jekshenkulov. Xi's upcoming visit will represent not only another milestone, but also an opportunity to elevate bilateral ties to a new level, he added. A MODEL OF FRIENDSHIP Since the establishment of diplomatic ties in 1956, China and Egypt have worked together to deepen their relationship, and strengthen friendship, solidarity and mutually beneficial cooperation. "China-Egypt relations have become a model of amity, solidarity and cooperation among developing countries, as well as a benchmark for collective cooperation between China and Arab states and between China and Africa, thereby advancing steadily toward building a China-Egypt community with a shared future in the new era," Xi said on May 30 in a congratulatory message to Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi on the 70th anniversary of diplomatic ties. Strong political trust and close engagement between the two leaders have been instrumental in driving bilateral ties. For over a decade, Xi and Sisi have met more than 10 times, providing strategic guidance for the continued expansion of bilateral cooperation. In 2014, the two countries elevated their relationship to a comprehensive strategic partnership. In 2016, Xi paid a state visit to Egypt. In 2024, Egypt became the first Arab country to include the goal of building a community with a shared future in a bilateral joint statement. A major symbol of this partnership is the China-Egypt Suez Economic and Trade Cooperation Zone. In January 2016, Xi and Sisi jointly inaugurated the second phase of the zone; it has since developed into a flagship project of China-Egypt industrial cooperation. By the end of June this year, the zone had attracted more than 200 companies, brought in over 4.7 billion U.S. dollars in investment, created more than 10,000 direct jobs and supported tens of thousands of additional job opportunities. Beyond economic cooperation, cultural exchanges have brought the two peoples ever closer together. Chinese language education has been introduced into Egypt's national education system, while growing interest in Chinese culture has encouraged more Egyptians to explore China. The exchange runs both ways: the Grand Egyptian Museum has become a magnet for Chinese tourists, while the Shanghai Museum's exhibition on ancient Egyptian civilization gave Chinese audiences a closer look at Egypt's rich cultural heritage in return. Egypt and China have developed a partnership rooted in mutual trust and understanding with remarkable resilience and vast potential for further development, said Osama El-Gohary, assistant to the Prime Minister of Egypt and chairman of the Information and Decision Support Center. Under the guidance of the two heads of state, Egypt-China ties are poised to reach new heights, delivering greater benefits to both peoples and contributing to global development, he said.■
